origin.description: Combine bootstrap objects that have the same components by stacking their replicate statistics.

arguments.text: Bootstrap objects. Each must have the same component names, in the same order.

arguments.name: recursive
arguments.text: Accepted because c() passes it. It is not used.

origin.details: The first object is kept. R is replaced by the sum of the replicate counts, and t is the row bind of every t matrix. Other components, including the seed and the call, stay those of the first object.
origin.value: A bootstrap object with the combined replicates.
origin.example:
set.seed(1)
stat <- function(d, i) mean(d[i])
b1 <- boot(1:10, stat, R = 10)
set.seed(2)
b2 <- boot(1:10, stat, R = 10)
c(b1, b2)

translation.description: Combine bootstrap objects that have the same components by stacking their replicate statistics.

arguments.name: args
arguments.text: BootResult objects. The component names must match, in order.

arguments.name: recursive
arguments.text: Accepted because R's c method receives it. It is not used.

translation.details: R becomes the sum of the replicate counts and t is stacked. The call, seed, and other components remain those of the first object.
translation.value: A BootResult with the combined replicates.
translation.example:
from boot.resample import boot, c_boot
from boot.rng import set_seed
import numpy as np

def stat(d, i):
    i = np.asarray(i, dtype=int)
    return float(np.mean(np.asarray(d)[i - 1]))

set_seed(1)
b1 = boot(np.arange(1, 11), stat, R=10)
set_seed(2)
b2 = boot(np.arange(1, 11), stat, R=10)
print(c_boot(b1, b2), end="")
